clusters.principle: A test that needs a system library gets it installed in CI and the dev environment, never mocked or skipped away.
Test data files stay small, trimmed to the records the test reads.
A fill value is a property of each variable or column, looked up per field, never assumed file-wide or defaulted.
Every timestamp read or written is UTC with a trailing Z, and anything else raises.
A check reviewers keep making by eye is enabled in the linter configuration, covering every file.
A comment describes what the code as it stands does, not past alternatives or history.
A daily product never drops a day; a day with no samples gets a filled row with n_samples 0.
No compatibility layers or shims for an installed base that does not exist yet.
The changelog records only changes a user of the package can observe.
Released changelog sections are frozen; new lines go under Unreleased.
A diff stays within what its ticket asks.
Config keys are snake_case everywhere, user YAML included.
When a change makes a test fail, the expected values are derived independently, never edited, loosened or regenerated from the code under test.
Rounding follows the product spec: half-up.
Float comparisons in tests use pytest.approx with an explicit rel or abs tolerance.
Open question: whether a daily mean needs a minimum sample count.
Type hints are not required on private helpers.
A failing lint check is fixed, and a noqa goes in only with a reason on the same line.
Every CI job pins the Python minor version.
csv_reader.read_station is the exemplar reader.
Findings about test helper names are not worth a review thread.
Below 1.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version.
A lookup that misses raises KeyError naming what was asked for, never returns None.
Open question: whether readers return xarray Datasets or pandas DataFrames.
Every written variable carries a units attribute, dimensionless ones included.
A writer refuses to overwrite an existing product rather than replacing it.
pytest runs with DeprecationWarning as an error.
File-handling functions take pathlib.Path and callers convert at the edge.
Station files are small enough that the proposed change is not needed.
